newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank sets baht reference at 27.383.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank sets baht reference at 27.383.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand on Thursday set its daily baht weighted average interbank rate at 27.383 to the dollar.
The reference rate was the first set by the central bank after it announced on Wednesday it would let the baht move according to a new managed float regime.
The baht was trading at 29.000/29.200 in the offshore market and 27.000 in the domestic market when the rate was announced.
The baht fell about 15 percent on Wednesday after Thailand abandoned its earlier long-standing practice of fixing the currency to a dollar-dominated basket of foreign currencies.
The daily reference rate is based on the baht's traded average on the previous business day.

Central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Wednesday the weighted average rate is announced primarily as a reference for tax and accounting purposes when private business deals with government agencies.
After the announcement the baht was trading lower than the Wednesday reference rate. At 0205 GMT it was trading at 29.20/29.50 offshore and 27.50/27.50 in local markets.

The Bank of Thailand also published a list of average rates quoted by commercial banks at the close of business. A central bank spokeswoman said the rates reflect the customer rate given at exchange counters.
